script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.

terra.problem: The dough comparison does not clearly match sailing around an island to shelter from opposing winds.
The closing observation about finding a boat going your direction is generic and adds little personality.
The explanation suggests Julius was persuaded because of the pilot's role, but the text does not give his reason.
It says Julius did not listen to the prisoners, although Paul was a prisoner who gave him advice. The text says Julius was persuaded contrary to that advice, not that he refused to listen.
The text says the lifeboat was hoisted up, but does not establish that it was impossible to tie it to the ship.
Saying he will not joke about the moment comments on how he is telling the passage.
Saying a bigger ship would not have fixed it makes a definite claim the text does not establish.
Paul says there will be no loss of life, but saying the people will be fine promises more than the text says.
The passages use the title Caesar, but do not explicitly establish that the same individual is meant in both places.
